2. Schema Conversion

  • Convert DB2 schema to PostgreSQL-compatible format.
  • Map data types (e.g., DECIMAL in DB2 to NUMERIC in PostgreSQL).
  • Recreate indexes, constraints, and relationships in PostgreSQL.

3. Data Migration

  • Extract data from DB2 using custom scripts, or ETL tools.
  • Transform data if needed (e.g., date formats, encoding).
  • Load data into PostgreSQL using COPY, INSERT, or ETL pipelines.

4. Code Migration

  • Rewrite DB2 stored procedures, functions, and triggers in PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL.
  • Validate logic and performance in the new environment.

5. Testing & Validation

  • Perform data integrity checks (row counts, checksums).
  • Validate application functionality against PostgreSQL.
  • Conduct performance benchmarking.

6. Cutover & Rollback Planning

  • Plan downtime or live migration strategy.
  • Prepare rollback procedures in case of failure.

7. Post-Migration Tasks

  • Monitor PostgreSQL performance.
  • Tune queries and indexes.
  • Set up backups and disaster recovery.

1. Pre-Migration Planning

  • Identify source and target PostgreSQL versions.
  • Assess compatibility (especially for major version upgrades).
  • Plan for zero-downtime migration if required.

2. Schema & Data Transfer

  • Use tools like pg_dump and pg_restore, or pg_basebackup for full cluster migration.
  • Ensure schema consistency and resolve version-specific changes.

3. Data Validation

  • Compare row counts, checksums, and sample data between source and target.
  • Validate indexes, constraints, and sequences.

4. Application Testing

  • Test application connectivity and functionality with the new database.
  • Validate performance and query plans.

5. Cutover Planning

  • Schedule cutover with minimal impact.
  • Ensure replication (if used) is in sync before switching.

6. Post-Migration Monitoring

  • Monitor logs, performance metrics, and error rates.
  • Tune PostgreSQL parameters for optimal performance.
